reason: Chevron-shaped glands and tertiary veins 'en chevrons' have the outline of a V; PATO:0002224 V-shaped covers it.

label: culm-like
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's resembling a culm: erect, stiff and narrow, so that it appears to continue the stem beyond the inflorescence. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0002457 leaf-like and FLOPO:0991200 bract-like; used of the lowest involucral bract of sedges.
reason: A standard sedge character (an involucral bract that looks like a continuation of the culm). No PATO or FLOPO term covers it, and it is a 'like'-shape in the same style as bract-like.
A degree adverb that modifies another value ('subdensely 6-9-flowered', 'subdensely tripinnate'). The flower count goes to pattern 03 and the division to its own term.
Arc-shaped / 'en forme d'arc' means curved like a bow. It is handled the same way as the earlier rule for arcuate (PATO:0000406 curved).
Didymous fruits are made of two equal rounded lobes: PATO:0002214 bilobed. The 'sub-' prefix is the approximate-value pattern.
Describes the nutrient supply of the habitat (peatland fed by groundwater), not a phenotype of the plant.
Degree of development of the moss peristome, meaningful only against 'reduced' in the same key. It is not a quality term in its own right, and PATO:0001701 mature does not fit.

label: longicidal
definition: A structural quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's opening at maturity by slits running along its length. NOTE: A kind of FLOPO:0991149 dehiscent; sibling of FLOPO:0991153 poricidal, used chiefly of anthers.
reason: The standard alternative to poricidal anther dehiscence. It belongs next to the dehiscence modes already in FLOPO.
An isocotylous embryo has cotyledons of equal size. The quality is FLOPO:0991102 equal, and the part it describes is the cotyledons, not the embryo.
French 'rostrée' (rostrate) keel = ending in a beak: FLOPO:0991028 beaked. The word 'rostered' is a mistranslation of rostrate.
French 'scléreux' = hardened by sclerenchyma (endocarp, leaf margin). It is handled the same way as the earlier rule for indurate (PATO:0000386 hard).
Effaced veins ('nervures effacées') are barely visible, which is handled the same way as obscure/indistinct (PATO:0000464).

target: new: compound of two values (strigose FLOPO:0991086 + sericeous PATO_0104358)
reason: A compound of two existing indumentum values (appressed stiff hairs that are silky). It needs the pattern for two run-together values, not a new term.

target: new: part of the bearer (vascular bundle PO_0005020 + low saturation PATO_0000328), docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1
reason: The quality belongs to the veins of the petal, not the petal. PATO:0000328 low saturation (synonym pale) on the veins, as part of the petal.

label: malpighiaceous
definition: A shape quality inhering in a hair by virtue of the hair's being attached at or near its middle, with two arms lying parallel to the surface. NOTE: Distinct from PATO:0001200 T-shaped, which does not require the arms to lie along the surface; used of Malpighiaceae, Cornaceae and Brassicaceae.
reason: A genuine trichome type used across several families. PATO has no term for a two-armed hair attached at its middle.
A rimlike calyx is reduced to a low ring round the top of the ovary, contrasted with 'lobed'. PATO:0002539 ring shaped (synonym annular) is the nearest existing term.
Clathrate = latticed (fern scales with thick dark cell walls; tertiary veins forming a lattice), so FLOPO:0991100 reticulate. The 'sub-' prefix is the approximate-value pattern.
Scapigerous = bearing a scape, which the earlier review mapped to peduncle (rule C255). So it means a peduncle is present, and 'sub-' is the approximate-value pattern.
Forming hummocks = growing in dense mounded tufts (grasses, mosses). FLOPO:0991007 caespitose (dense tufts or clumps) is the closest existing value, and the size of the mound stays in the text.
There is no term for a metallic lustre, and negating PATO:0001373 glistening would be wrong (the plant may still be shiny). It is a key contrast that means little alone.

target: new: part of the bearer (trichome PO_0000282 + tuberculate FLOPO:0991060 at its base), docs/annotation-context-patterns.md slot 1
reason: 'Poils tuberculés à la base' = hairs with a swollen base. The quality belongs to the base of the hairs, which needs the part-of-the-bearer slot, not a new indumentum term.
'Sub-' plus an existing FLOPO value (scarious) is the approximate-value pattern.
An M-shaped leaf blade in cross section is the W profile seen from the other side. Read relative to the blade, it is PATO:0002439 w-shaped.
Fistulose = hollow like a pipe: PATO:0002078 hollow. 'Not fistulose' is its negation.

label: apogamous
definition: A reproductive quality inhering in a plant by virtue of its sporophyte arising directly from the gametophyte without fertilization. NOTE: Probably outside PATO's scope (a mode of reproduction); kept in FLOPO for ferns, beside the sexual qualities.
reason: A standard fern character, given together with the chromosome number. No PATO term for it was found.

label: biturbinate
definition: A 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like two tops joined at their broad ends: widest at the middle and tapering to each end. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991077 turbinate.
reason: A fruit shape distinct from turbinate (which tapers to one end only), and no existing term covers it.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (position along costule = vascular bundle PO_0005020)
reason: 'Sori costular' = sori placed along the costules. This relates the sorus to another part (costule, rule C394), so it uses the relation pattern.
Says that old leaf sheaths do not persist as fibres at the stem base. Writing it as 'leaf sheath absent' would be false, and it is a key contrast rather than a term.

target: new: depth of division (split PATO_0001786 to a stated level)
reason: 'Parted nearly to base/middle' says how far a calyx or corolla is divided. That is split (PATO:0001786) plus a position, which needs a depth-of-division pattern.
Faintly visible veins = barely visible: PATO:0000464 inconspicuous (related synonym faint, as in rule C326).
